newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HKMA says stable currency most important 1997 job.
newsitem.headline: HKMA says stable currency most important 1997 job.

text.p: Hong Kong's de facto central bank chief said on Wednesday the most important task of the monetary authority in 1997 would be maintaining exchange rate stability.
"The most important thing is to keep the currency stable," said Joseph Yam, chief executive of Hong Kong Monetary Authority at his yearend news conference.

In a review of the authority's major achievements this year and tasks coming up in 1997, Yam said exchange rate stability was the foremost task, followed by the need to maintain a steady and healthy banking sector.
The establishment of the Hong Kong Mortgage Corp Ltd was another major task for 1997, he said.
The authority has prepared a draft memorandum on the structure and scope of operation of the corporation and will circulate this among banks in Hong Kong for consultation next month.
Yam said that once the corporation was operational it would be removed from the authority and act independently. The authority hopes to have it up and running in second half 1997.
The aim is to create a secondary market in home mortgages similar to the U.S. Ginnie Mae market.
Another major task in 1997 will be hosting the 1997 World Bank/IMF annual meeting to be held in Hong Kong in September 1997, Yam said.

The meeting, which will be held after the territory reverts to Chinese sovereignty, will be a showcase event for Beijing and the first time China has hosted such a high profile international financial conference.
Other major tasks Yam outlined were supervision of smart cards and developing policy on other technological innovations.

Yam said milestones in 1996 were the implementation of a real time gross settlement (RTGS) system for banks, the establishment of the U.S. Federal Funds rate as the reference rate for liquid adjustment facility (LAF) rate, the issue of 10-year exchange fund notes, and joining the Bank for International Settlements (BIS).
